description: Multi-dimensional adversarial review of a diff or capability: correctness, security, and spec compliance, with every finding adversarially verified before it is reported.

args.scope: Phase 6 QA proof frontend (qa-phase6-ui): the recording clips e2e/recordings/admin-and-theme.spec.ts, playwright.record.config.ts, tools/record-e2e-clips.mjs (Playwright JSON report -> recordings manifest), the e2e suite's testIgnore, and the product fix in src/features/missions/MissionEditorScreen.tsx (refetch the topic task list after a publish/unpublish or a refused status change) with its unit test
args.focus: Do the clips really ASSERT each FR they claim in their proof annotation (FR-1, FR-2, FR-4, FR-6, FR-7, FR-8, FR-10, FR-11, FR-13, FR-39, FR-40, FR-41, FR-58; requirement text in contract/docs/requirements.md) rather than just mentioning it? Can tools/record-e2e-clips.mjs ever write asserted: true for a failed, skipped, flaky or missing clip, or a manifest entry without a video/still on disk (scripts/check-recordings.mjs contract)? Is the mission editor fix correct (TanStack Query key prefixes, TASKS_KEY vs ['admin','task']), does it cause a stale or racing state, and does the new test fail without it? No real names/PII or workbook content in fixtures or stills (NFR-3/NFR-4).

findings.title: rec-task-list-provenance claims FR-11 but never exercises the grade, topic or modality filters
findings.evidence: FR-11 says 'Admin filters and searches tasks by grade, topic, source, page, modality, and status'. The clip only drives `admin.tasks.source`, `admin.tasks.status`, `admin.tasks.page` and `admin.tasks.search` (lines 156-163). It never touches grade, topic or modality, yet `proves('FR-11, FR-13')` makes the manifest record FR-11 as asserted.
findings.suggestion: Add steps that pick a grade, a topic and a modality, each followed by a row-count/content assertion against the seed. If you'd rather not, narrow the proof annotation and record the rest of FR-11 as covered elsewhere, citing that test.

findings.title: rec-skin-hq claims FR-39 but does not assert that the skin is swappable
findings.evidence: FR-39 is 'The theme (names, ranks, copy, illustrations, colors) is one swappable skin'. The clip only checks that the HQ shows `PLACEHOLDER_LADDER[0].name` and that the body text has no deny-listed term. Those are IP-rule checks; nothing shows the rank names, copy or colours come from one skin module that can be replaced (for example, a second ladder or skin rendering different names).
findings.suggestion: Make the backend return a different ladder (or inject an alternate skin) and assert that the HQ rank and copy change with it. Alternatively, mark FR-39 here as partial and point to the unit test that proves swappability.

findings.title: Manifest entry always lists a screenshot path, even when no still was attached
findings.evidence: `if (still) copyFileSync(still, out('png'));` only copies when an attachment exists, but `results.push({... screenshot: out('png'), asserted ...})` writes the path unconditionally. scripts/check-recordings.mjs line 100 treats a missing screenshot only as `warn`. So a passing clip that skipped `still()`, or a refactor that renames the attachment, gets `asserted: true` with a .png path that does not exist on disk. The same happens with `video` (line 45), although the checker does fail on a missing video.
findings.suggestion: Mark the clip as failed (`asserted: false` with an error, and count it in `failed`) when the video or still attachment is missing or the copied file is empty. Write `screenshot`/`video` only when the copy actually happened.

findings.title: Clips that don't match the title regex are silently dropped, and the tool doesn't check for expected clips
findings.evidence: `if (!run || !match) continue;` drops any spec with no result or with a title that no longer matches `/^(rec-[\w-]+): (.*)$/`, without counting it as failed. The tool also doesn't check the result against a list of expected clip ids or FRs. A renamed, deleted or never-run clip therefore just disappears from the manifest, which is rebuilt from scratch after `rmSync(OUT_DIR)`, and the run still exits 0 as long as at least one clip passed. Global errors in `report.errors` and the `spawnSync` exit status are ignored too.
findings.suggestion: Count unmatched or result-less specs as failures. Keep an expected list of clip ids (or FRs), fail when one is missing, and also fail on non-empty `report.errors`.

findings.title: Flaky clips would count as asserted if retries were ever enabled
findings.evidence: `const run = spec.tests[0]?.results?.at(-1); ... const asserted = run.status === 'passed';` only looks at the last attempt. playwright.record.config.ts sets `retries: 0` today. But if retries are enabled (via the config or a `--retries` CLI flag), a clip that failed and then passed on retry (`spec.tests[0].status === 'flaky'`) gets `asserted: true` and the video from the passing retry. Only `spec.tests[0]` is read, so extra projects are ignored as well.
findings.suggestion: Require `spec.tests[0].status === 'expected'` and `results.length === 1` (or all results passed). Treat 'flaky', 'skipped' and 'unexpected' as not asserted.

findings.title: FR-7 and FR-8 claims leave parts of the requirement unasserted (hint-less task, part-label translation)
findings.evidence: FR-7 includes 'Tasks without hints work normally', and FR-8 covers translations of 'prompt, part labels, and hints'. The clip asserts three ordered hints, the uk prompt (which was already seeded, not entered in this clip) and uk hint 1. It never enters or asserts a translated part label, and never shows a task with zero hints.
findings.suggestion: Fill and assert a `uk` part-label translation, and enter (or assert the existing) uk prompt in the flow. For FR-7, add a preview of a seeded hint-less task, or reference the test that covers it.

findings.title: rec-source-upload never sets grade or subject; it relies on form defaults
findings.evidence: FR-1 is about the admin entering title, publisher, edition, grade and subject. The clip fills the title, types publisher and edition by tabbing blindly (`keyboard.press('Tab')` then `type`), and submits. The backend assertion `grade: 6, subject: 'math'` passes only because those are the defaults, so the clip doesn't show the admin choosing a grade or subject. The tab-order typing also depends on field order rather than labels.
findings.suggestion: Select a non-default grade and subject through their labelled controls, fill publisher and edition with `getByLabel`, and assert those chosen values in `backend.sources[0].source`.

findings.title: New unit test doesn't cover the refused-publish refetch path
findings.evidence: The fix adds `await refreshTaskRows();` in the `changeStatus` catch block (MissionEditorScreen.tsx:161). The test only flips `backend.tasks` to PUBLISHED after the first refusal, so the refetch it observes is triggered by the successful second publish through `refresh()`. Removing line 161 would still leave the test green. The RED run documented in docs/qa/evidence/phase6-red-run.md only proves the success-path fix. Apart from this, the fix itself is correct: TASKS_KEY `['admin','tasks']` prefix-matches the `useTasks` key `[...TASKS_KEY, filters]`, which `['admin','task']` did not.
findings.suggestion: Add a case where the tasks change before a publish that is refused (for example, one task becomes PUBLISHED while another stays DRAFT). Assert that the rows update after the refusal. Confirm it fails without line 161.

findings.title: Mission delete still leaves the topic task rows and task-list missionIds stale
findings.evidence: `destroy()` invalidates `MISSIONS_KEY` and `['admin','task']`, but unlike `refresh()` it doesn't call `refreshTaskRows()`. `['admin','task']` does not prefix-match `['admin','tasks', filters]`, so the cached task list (which shows mission membership) keeps the deleted mission's id until the cache is refetched for another reason. It's the same key bug this change fixes for publish.
findings.suggestion: Call `refreshTaskRows()` (that is, invalidate `TASKS_KEY`) in `destroy()` as well, or move all mission-mutation invalidations into one helper.

findings.title: rec-parts-hints-translations claims FR-8 but only proves entering one hint translation; the prompt translation is seed data and part-label translations are never asserted
findings.evidence: FR-8 requires translations of the prompt, the part labels and the hints. The only thing the clip types is the uk translation of hint 1 (line 189). The assertion on `translations.uk.prompt` (line 201) checks a value already in the stub seed (src/test/fake-admin-backend.ts:129), so it passes even if the editor cannot edit prompt translations. `translations.uk.partLabels` is never filled in or checked. The manifest still marks FR-8 as asserted.
findings.suggestion: In the clip, fill a new uk prompt translation and a uk label for the new part, and assert both in `backend.tasks[...].input.translations.uk`. Otherwise drop FR-8 from the proof annotation.

findings.title: rec-source-upload claims grade and subject for FR-1 but never sets them; it only checks stub defaults
findings.evidence: The test title says the source is uploaded 'with title, publisher, edition, grade and subject', but the flow only fills the file, title, publisher (via Tab) and edition. `toMatchObject({ grade: 6, subject: 'math' })` passes on the form defaults. A broken grade or subject selector would still produce `asserted: true` for FR-1.
findings.suggestion: Pick a grade and subject that differ from the defaults (e.g. select another subject or grade), then assert the stored values. Use labelled locators instead of positional Tab presses, so a change in field order fails loudly.

findings.title: FR-2 and FR-4 clips skip part of the requirement ('side by side'; 'shown to the child')
findings.evidence: FR-2 requires the PDF to be viewed side by side with the editor. The clip asserts page navigation and that the form keeps its content, but nothing about layout: a viewer stacked below the editor would still pass. FR-4 requires images to be shown to the child with the task, but rec-task-images (line 173) only checks the admin preview (`/admin/tasks/preview`), not a child route. Vision review partly covers this, but the `asserted` flag claims more than the code asserts.
findings.suggestion: For FR-2, compare the bounding boxes of the viewer canvas and the editor form (e.g. viewer.right <= form.left and overlapping vertical ranges). For FR-4, either assert the images on the child task screen via childBackend, or cite the e2e spec that covers the child rendering in the explainer.

findings.title: FR-11 and FR-58 assertions are narrower than the requirement
findings.evidence: FR-11 lists filters by grade, topic, source, page, modality and status. The clip exercises source, status, page and text search, but not grade, topic or modality. FR-58's 'no in-app toggle' check only looks for `[data-theme], .dk-toggle, [role=switch]`, so a theme toggle built as a plain `<button>` (e.g. 'Dark mode') would pass.
findings.suggestion: Add the topic and modality filters to the FR-11 clip, or narrow its proof text. For FR-58, also assert that no button or link has an accessible name matching /theme|dark|light|tmav|světl/i.

findings.title: Recorder can mark a clip asserted while its screenshot is missing, and silently drops clips that have no result
findings.evidence: The tool always writes `screenshot: out('png')`, even when no still was attached. scripts/check-recordings.mjs:100 only warns when a screenshot is missing, so a passing clip without a still would yield a manifest entry with `asserted: true` that points at a file that does not exist. Separately, specs with no result or a non-`rec-` title are skipped with `continue`, and the spawnSync exit code is ignored. A clip renamed or lost from the report then just disappears instead of failing the run. Failed and skipped clips are correctly written as false (status !== 'passed'). Flaky clips can't be marked passed while retries=0, but `results.at(-1)` would take a passing retry if retries are ever raised. A missing video makes check-recordings fail, so that case is not a false pass.
findings.suggestion: Set `asserted` only when status === 'passed' AND the video and still were both copied (existsSync after the copy), and only list paths that exist. Count a missing result or an unparseable title as a failure, or check the spawnSync status. Use `run.retry === 0` or reject `outcome === 'flaky'` so a pass after retry never counts.

findings.title: The refused-publish task-list refresh (catch branch) has no test: removing it keeps the suite green
findings.evidence: The new test mutates the backend only after the refused publish, then publishes successfully. Only the success path (`refresh` → `refreshTaskRows`) is checked. Without the fix, the success-path assertion at line 411 does fail, because `['admin','task']` does not prefix-match `['admin','tasks', filters]` (TASKS_KEY = ['admin','tasks']), so the rows would stay stale. But deleting `await refreshTaskRows()` at MissionEditorScreen.tsx:161 would pass every test. Otherwise the fix is correct: it invalidates the right prefix, invalidateQueries does not throw, and `busy` stays true until the refetch finishes, so no racing double-submit.
findings.suggestion: Add a case: set the backend tasks to PUBLISHED (simulating another tab), click Publish so it is refused for another reason or the status is now stale, and assert the rows show Published without a second publish.

findings.title: Security checklist: no issues in this diff (authz, auth/session, injection, exposure, secrets, dependencies, PII/workbook)
findings.evidence: Authz/IDOR/mass assignment: this range changes no backend, API or generated-client code. The only product change is a client-side cache invalidation, which adds no endpoint and changes no data the child surface sees. Auth/session: no change; the clips sign in through the existing stubbed `signedInAdmin` fixture with no credentials in code. Injection: `painter.setContent` uses constant self-authored HTML in a test-only page, and the recorder writes files only under fixed OUT_DIR / test-results-record paths taken from the Playwright report, so no user input reaches a path. Exposure: `vite preview --port 4181 --strictPort` binds to localhost by default, and test-results-record/ is gitignored. Secrets: no env or VITE_* additions. Dependencies: package.json only adds a script and package-lock.json is unchanged, so this diff adds no new advisory surface (npm audit was not run). NFR-3/NFR-4: fixtures and stills use self-authored stub data ('Testovací nakladatelství', generic decimal and perimeter prompts, coloured '1'/'2' PNGs drawn at runtime). No child name, photo or workbook text or images were found.
findings.suggestion: None required. Note that rerunning tools/record-e2e-clips.mjs deletes OUT_DIR and rewrites manifest.json without the `vision` blocks that are now committed, so re-run vision-verify after any re-record.

findings.title: Coverage summary (FRs claimed by the Phase 6 clips plus the mission editor fix)
findings.evidence: 14 scenarios: 9 implemented, 5 partial, 0 missing, 0 contradicted. Fully asserted: FR-4, FR-6, FR-7, FR-10, FR-13, FR-40, FR-41, FR-58, and the mission editor refetch. Partial: FR-1 (grade and subject never chosen), FR-2 (side-by-side layout not asserted), FR-8 (prompt translation is seed data; part-label translation absent), FR-11 (3 of 6 filter dimensions), FR-39 (swappability not asserted).
findings.suggestion: See the individual findings.

findings.title: FR-39 clip asserts the IP deny-list, not a swappable skin
findings.evidence: FR-39: "The theme (names, ranks, copy, illustrations, colors) is one swappable **skin**." The clip only checks `panel.getByText(PLACEHOLDER_LADDER[0].name)` and `findDenied(bodyText, terms)).toEqual([])`. Nothing shows that the names, ranks, copy and colours come from one replaceable skin unit. For example, it never swaps the ladder or skin and checks that the UI follows. The deny-list check is the IP rule, not FR-39.
findings.suggestion: Make the clip serve a second, different ladder or skin from the stub, then assert that HQ renders the new rank names. Alternatively, narrow the `proves('FR-39')` claim and record which mechanism proves swappability.

findings.title: FR-11 clip covers only source, status, page and text search; grade, topic and modality filters are not asserted
findings.evidence: FR-11: "Admin filters and searches tasks by grade, topic, source, page, modality, and status." The clip sets only `admin.tasks.source`, `admin.tasks.status` and `admin.tasks.page` together (`toHaveCount(2)`), plus a search. It never uses the grade, topic or modality filters. It checks only row counts, not that the remaining rows match each filter.
findings.suggestion: Exercise the grade, topic and modality filters one at a time and assert the rows' content, or reduce the proof claim and point to the e2e spec that covers the rest.

findings.title: FR-8 clip enters only a hint translation; the prompt translation it asserts is pre-seeded and part-label translation is absent
findings.evidence: FR-8: "Admin adds translations of prompt, part labels, and hints per locale (`uk`)". The clip fills only `admin.editor.trHint` n:1. It then asserts `saved.translations?.uk?.prompt).toBe('Запиши одну половину…')`, which is the stub's seed value (the preview clip shows the same string before any edit), so it is not an admin action. Part-label translations are never entered or asserted.
findings.suggestion: Fill the uk prompt and the uk part-label fields in the clip with new values and assert that they are persisted.

findings.title: FR-1 clip never selects grade or subject; it asserts the form defaults
findings.evidence: FR-1 asks for upload "with metadata: title, publisher, edition, grade, and subject". The clip fills the file and title, Tabs into publisher and edition, then presses Enter. It asserts `grade: 6, subject: 'math'` on the backend, but these are whatever the form pre-fills, not the admin's choice. Relying on Tab order also makes the clip fragile.
findings.suggestion: Use labelled fields for publisher and edition, and explicitly select a grade and subject (ideally non-default ones) before asserting.

findings.title: FR-2 'side by side with the task editor' is not asserted
findings.evidence: FR-2: "views an uploaded PDF page by page, side by side with the task editor, and can jump to a page number". The clip asserts page navigation and that the form keeps its value. It does not assert that the viewer and editor are laid out side by side (e.g. bounding boxes). The vision note says the editor Page field reads 57 while the viewer shows 30.
findings.suggestion: Add a bounding-box assertion (viewer.x + viewer.width <= editor.x, overlapping y) at 1280×720.

findings.title: record-e2e-clips silently drops expected clips that are missing from the report
findings.evidence: `if (!run || !match) continue;` skips any spec with no result or without the `rec-` prefix. The tool fails only when `results.length === 0`. playwright.record.config.ts has no `forbidOnly`, so a stray `test.only`, `--grep` or renamed title would drop clips. The tool would then exit 0, wipe the old evidence (`rmSync(OUT_DIR)`) and write a smaller manifest. The FR proof would simply disappear, and check-traceability is the only backstop.
findings.suggestion: Treat a spec without a run or without the `rec-` prefix as a failure. Set `forbidOnly: true` in playwright.record.config.ts and/or check against an expected clip list. Also check that the spawnSync exit status agrees with `failed`.

findings.title: An asserted clip can be written with no video or still on disk
findings.evidence: `if (video) copyFileSync(...)` / `if (still) copyFileSync(...)` copy files only when attachments exist. Yet `results.push({... video: out('webm'), screenshot: out('png'), asserted })` always writes both paths, and `asserted` depends only on `run.status === 'passed'`. check-recordings.mjs FAILs a missing video, but only WARNs on a missing screenshot (`if (!shotOk) warn(...)`), so a passed clip with no still goes green.
findings.suggestion: Set `asserted` to false (or exit 1) when the video or still attachment is absent, and make the explainer report it. Flaky or skipped clips are already handled: retries are 0 and `status !== 'passed'` gives `asserted: false`.

findings.title: Re-running the recorder wipes the vision verdicts stored in the committed manifest
findings.evidence: The committed docs/qa/demo-recordings/phase6-admin-theme/manifest.json has a `vision` block on each clip. The tool does `rmSync(OUT_DIR, …)` and writes results without `vision`. The committed manifest therefore can't be reproduced by the tool, and any re-record silently drops G6 vision evidence.
findings.suggestion: Carry existing vision verdicts forward only when the clip is unchanged, or document that vision-verify must be re-run after every re-record.

findings.title: Proposal says 'No product behaviour changes' but the slice ships a product fix in MissionEditorScreen
findings.evidence: proposal.md: "No product behaviour changes" and "Capabilities: None changed: QA tooling and evidence only." The diff changes src/features/missions/MissionEditorScreen.tsx: refresh() and the refused-status catch now invalidate TASKS_KEY. The commit carries `Refs: FR-9`.
findings.suggestion: Amend proposal.md and tasks.md to list the MissionEditor fix (FR-9, vision-verify finding on slice6-mission-create-reorder-publish), its unit test and the RED evidence.

findings.title: Ticked tasks 3.1–3.3 have no artifacts: no review-findings.json, current-state not updated, qa:verify not re-run after the code change
findings.evidence: `- [x] 3.1 … findings dispositioned in review-findings.json`: openspec/changes/qa-phase6-ui/ has only design.md, proposal.md and tasks.md. `- [x] 3.3 docs/current-state.md updated`: the file still reads `Current phase: Phase 5` / `Last completed gate: G3` and is not in the diff. `- [x] 3.2 npm run qa:verify; npm run test:e2e:stack at the final code commit`: automated-verification-latest.md and e2e-stack-latest.md were last changed at abd8c60/e538936, before the product fix in fa56996.
findings.suggestion: Untick 3.1–3.3 until the artifacts exist, or produce them: write review-findings.json, update current-state.md with evidence pointers, and re-run qa:verify and the stack E2E at the final commit. Treat the false ticks as a correction event (done-claims-need-evidence).

findings.title: Mission editor fix is correct, but the refused-status refetch path has no test
findings.evidence: The fix is correct. `useTasks` uses `[...TASKS_KEY, filters]` = ['admin','tasks',{topicId}], and the old `['admin','task']` prefix never matched it because prefix matching is per element. The invalidation is awaited inside `busy`, so I see no race. The new test is RED without the fix (docs/qa/evidence/phase6-red-run.md). However, it flips the backend tasks to PUBLISHED after the refusal and only asserts after the successful publish. The `catch { …; await refreshTaskRows(); }` branch is never shown to refresh rows on its own: removing that line would keep the test green.
findings.suggestion: Add a test where the tasks are published elsewhere, publish is still refused (e.g. a different blocker), and the rows update after the refusal. Alternatively, drop the catch-path refetch if it has no requirement behind it.

findings.title: FR-58 'no in-app toggle' check uses a narrow selector heuristic
findings.evidence: FR-58: "there is no in-app toggle in MVP". The clip asserts `page.locator('[data-theme], .dk-toggle, [role=switch]')).toHaveCount(0)`. A toggle built as a plain button, a checkbox or a select (e.g. 'Dark mode') would pass. The light/dark background assertions themselves are sound.
findings.suggestion: Also assert there is no button, checkbox or option whose accessible name matches /theme|dark|light|tmav|svět/i.

findings.title: FR-39 clip does not assert the requirement (one swappable skin)
findings.evidence: FR-39: 'The theme (names, ranks, copy, illustrations, colors) is one swappable skin.' rec-skin-hq only checks that HQ shows PLACEHOLDER_LADDER[0].name and that the page has no IP deny-list term (lines 182-185). It never shows that the skin is one swappable unit: nothing swaps the ladder or skin, and nothing checks that names, copy, illustrations or colours come from a single skin source. The deny-list check proves the IP rule, not FR-39. The manifest still records `asserted: true` for FR-39.
findings.suggestion: Make the clip swap the skin, for example by serving a second ladder/skin fixture from childBackend, and assert that rank names, copy and the colour token change together. Alternatively, narrow the proof annotation to what the clip does prove and cover FR-39 with its local-verifiable method.

findings.title: FR-11 clip covers only 3 of the 6 required filters (grade, topic and modality are never used)
findings.evidence: FR-11 requires filtering and searching by grade, topic, source, page, modality and status. The clip uses only the source, status and page selects plus the search box (lines 156-164). The grade, topic and modality filters are never used, yet the clip is annotated as proving FR-11.
findings.suggestion: Also select grade, topic and modality, and assert each narrows the row count. Otherwise annotate the clip as a partial proof and point to the e2e spec that covers the rest.

findings.title: FR-8 / FR-6 assertions partly check seed data, not admin input; translated part labels never asserted
findings.evidence: `saved.translations?.uk?.prompt` equals the seeded prompt; the clip never types it, so it passes without any authoring. FR-8 also requires translated part labels, which are never filled or asserted (the editor has a 'Label of part N (uk)' field). The check `parts.map(p => p.label).every(l => l.length > 0)` would pass on default labels. For FR-7, the 'tasks without hints work normally' half is not shown.
findings.suggestion: Fill and assert the uk prompt and the uk label of part 2 typed in the clip. Assert the exact part labels (['a','b']). Optionally save or preview a task with zero hints for FR-7.

findings.title: FR-1 clip never chooses grade/subject and fills publisher/edition by blind Tab order
findings.evidence: Publisher and edition are typed after `keyboard.press('Tab')`, without targeting their labelled fields. Grade 6 and subject 'math' are asserted in the backend payload but come from form defaults, so the recording never shows the admin entering grade or subject. A field reorder could also put the text into the wrong inputs, and the clip would still pass if the defaults happened to match.
findings.suggestion: Fill publisher and edition through getByLabel, and explicitly select grade and subject (a non-default value) before asserting the payload.

findings.title: FR-4 'shown to the child' is asserted only in the admin preview; JPG never exercised
findings.evidence: The image order is checked on /admin/tasks/preview, not in the child task screen. FR-4 says the images are shown to the child with the task and allows PNG/JPG, but only PNG is uploaded.
findings.suggestion: Either open the task in the child app (via childBackend) and assert the [data-image-id] order there, or state in the explainer that the preview stands in for the child view (FR-10). Add one JPEG upload.

findings.title: FR-58 'no in-app toggle' check uses a narrow selector
findings.evidence: The clip checks `[data-theme], .dk-toggle, [role=switch]` has count 0. A theme toggle built as a plain button, checkbox or select (e.g. 'Dark mode') would not match, so the assertion is weak evidence for 'no in-app toggle'.
findings.suggestion: Also assert no button, checkbox or select has an accessible name matching /theme|dark|light|tmav|světl/i.

findings.title: record-e2e-clips silently drops specs without results or a non-matching title; no expected clip list
findings.evidence: `if (!run || !match) continue;` skips a spec without counting it as failed. A clip that never ran (worker crash, interruption, maxFailures) or whose title lost its `rec-` prefix vanishes from the manifest, and the run can still exit 0 if the other clips pass. Duplicate ids overwrite each other's files. spawnSync's exit status and report.errors (top-level or load errors) are ignored. A failed, skipped or flaky clip cannot get asserted:true: the check is status === 'passed' and retries is 0.
findings.suggestion: Count `!run`, and any spec in e2e/recordings without a rec- id, as a failure. Fail on duplicate ids and on a non-empty report.errors. Ideally compare against an expected list of clip ids or FRs so a missing clip fails the run.

findings.title: Manifest entry claims video/still paths even when no attachment exists
findings.evidence: `video: out('webm'), screenshot: out('png')` are written whether or not `video` or `still` was found and copied, and `asserted` depends only on the test status. scripts/check-recordings.mjs catches this (lines 92-99 check that the video exists and meets a minimum size, and that the screenshot exists), so the gate is safe. The tool still emits an inconsistent `asserted: true` entry with dangling paths, and the explainer links a still that may not exist.
findings.suggestion: If the video or still attachment is missing, set asserted:false with an error ('no video'/'no still') and count it as failed.

findings.title: Refused-status refetch path (catch → refreshTaskRows) is not covered by a test
findings.evidence: The fix is correct: TanStack prefix matching means ['admin','task'] does not match TASKS_KEY ['admin','tasks', filters], so the new invalidateQueries({queryKey: TASKS_KEY}) is needed. The awaits are sequential, and the work runs inside busy=true, so no race was found. The new test changes task status only after the refused publish and asserts fresh rows after the successful publish, so it covers only refresh(). Deleting `await refreshTaskRows()` at MissionEditorScreen.tsx:161 would not fail any test. (I could not run git or the tests; that the test fails without the fix is inferred from the key mismatch.)
findings.suggestion: Add a case where the tasks are published elsewhere, then publish is refused for another reason (e.g. a stub 409 on a different blocker), and assert the rows refresh to Published after the refusal.

result.reasoning:
